summary: Remote WebSocket-driven PTY shell and localhost tunnel to hardcoded relay
details: When the `agentlink-client start` CLI is invoked, the package opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded relay at wss://msclaude.ai and routes inbound messages into a PTY spawned as `/bin/bash` on POSIX or `powershell.exe` on Windows in the user's working directory (dist/terminal.js: pty.spawn(shell, [], { env: {...process.env, AGENTLINK_PID:... } }); dist/connection.js dispatches `terminal_input` frames to `terminalManager.write(msg.data)`). Any party holding the session URL — whose end-to-end key is embedded in the URL fragment shared through the relay — can drive the shell with the running user's privileges. The same WebSocket channel accepts `tunnel_request` / `tunnel_ws_open` frames and forwards them to 127.0.0.1:<port> on the host (dist/tunnel.js: http.request({ hostname: '127.0.0.1', port, method, path, headers: forwardHeaders })), with the port allowlist mutated at runtime by `proxy_config_update` messages arriving on the same relay-controlled channel, exposing local dev servers, admin UIs, and other loopback-bound services to the relay-connected browser. The relay hostname is hardcoded and not the installer's infrastructure; a compromise or malicious operation of that relay yields full remote code execution under the invoking user's account plus reachability of any loopback service on the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
